items: 48 V split-phase 120/240 V inverter-charger that charges from the grid (Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V)
48 V (51.2 V) server-rack LiFePO4 batteries, 2-pack for 10.24 kWh or 4-pack for 20.48 kWh (Sun Gold Power SG48100P)
DC breaker sized for the battery-to-inverter run (Sun Gold Power 160 A)
48 VDC bus bar to parallel the batteries (Sun Gold Power 250 A)
why: ChatGPT's answer is built around sizing: it sets out a 1/2/3-battery cost table and a runtime calculator, and it warns that whole-home backup needs extra control equipment. The only products it carded were the single installer-sold Powerwall 3 and FranklinWH aPower 2, and neither is a grid-charged set you can buy in one cart. A grid-charging system without solar only works if a split-phase 120/240 V inverter-charger is matched to 48 V batteries and to a DC breaker and bus bar rated for about 125 A of continuous draw at 6 kW. One Sun Gold Power cart holds that set in two sizes, roughly 10 kWh for essentials versus 20 kWh for a full day or longer, which matches the tradeoff in ChatGPT's table. The page should also say that a licensed electrician must install a transfer switch or critical-loads panel, and that part is not in the cart.
